Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
News reports about events similar to what happened to me
push away positive emotions because they feel unsafe

Memory.value: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: The people responsible have faced no consequences
I should have protected others and I failed
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: For a trauma type of witnessed other trauma, the appraisal that others can see what happened to me by looking at me is hard to reconcile unless there was also direct victimization or visible injury. The rest of the profile centers on witnessing, guilt about failing to protect, and anger that perpetrators were not held accountable, which fits. This item implies a conspicuous personal mark or shame signal not otherwise supported by the triggers, memory, or strategies, so it is clinically incoherent within this profile.

vignette: Sofia, a 70-year-old Latin American woman and retired fashion designer, has been struggling with the aftermath of witnessing a traumatic event. The incident occurred several years ago when she was visiting her daughter in another city. She witnessed an accident that took the life of someone close to her, which left her feeling deeply unsettled and unable to cope. Since then, Sofia has experienced persistent triggers that have significantly impacted her daily life. A specific temperature on her skin or a news report about events similar to what she witnessed can instantly bring back the full memory in vivid detail. These triggers not only activate uncontrolled access to the traumatic memories but also cause her intense distress and feelings of loss of control. Sofia's memory is particularly intrusive; when the event comes back, it feels completely real across all her senses at once. She has learned that something in her surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning, leaving her feeling overwhelmed and vulnerable. The intensity of these memories often leads to a cycle where she becomes increasingly aware of her inability to control them, reinforcing her negative appraisals. What frightens Sofia most is the belief that the people responsible for the accident have faced no consequences. This has led her to question her own role in the event, feeling that she should have protected others and failed. These thoughts contribute to a deep sense of self-blame, which in turn exacerbates her negative appraisals and makes it more likely for her memories to be triggered. Sofia’s coping strategies include avoiding anything that reminds her of the loss, such as news reports or even positive emotions because they feel unsafe. However, these avoidance behaviors have only served to reinforce her triggers rather than alleviate them. For example, she avoids watching the news altogether but finds herself increasingly sensitive to temperature changes and other reminders in her environment. Her husband has noticed a significant change in Sofia's behavior over time; she is more withdrawn and less engaged with activities they once enjoyed together. At work, as a fashion designer, she often struggles with focusing on projects that remind her of the traumatic event, leading to feelings of frustration and guilt about not being able to protect others. The realization that her avoidance behaviors were making things worse finally compelled Sofia to seek help. She is most afraid that she will never be able to fully escape the memory and the overwhelming emotions it brings. However, she hopes that with support, she can regain some control over her life and find a way to live without being constantly haunted by the traumatic event. Sofia's journey has been marked by a self-reinforcing cycle where her triggers lead to maladaptive strategies, which in turn heighten her sensitivity to further triggers. The intensity of her memories and the negative appraisals she holds about herself have created a persistent sense of threat that permeates her daily life. Despite these challenges, Sofia remains hopeful that with the right support, she can break this cycle and find peace.
